title: ccw-heavyweight
label: The Supreme Machine

won.source: The fed's own history, carried on Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

how: Reclaimed it at SuMa's Destruction, a pay-per-view named for him and given to him as the reward for winning the first Champions of the Ring tournament; the fed's own history calls it his last Heavyweight Title run. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: Nothing held says how the belt left him.

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Phil Burner

won.source: The fed's own history, carried on Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

how: Beat Tim Inman at Showdown I for his first Heavyweight Championship, and held it what the fed's own history calls a record 104 days. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Phil Burner

won.source: The fed's own history, carried on Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

how: Won the Champions of the Ring tournament and the Heavyweight Title in one night, the second time that tournament made a champion outright. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: He was running the federation by October of the same year, after its founder was announced dead; nothing held says how the belt left him.

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Blayze

won.source: The fed's own heavyweight title history (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/heavyweight-title-history-2003.html): "Awarded (Still reigning)", 02-06-2003, Iowa City, Ia.

how: Awarded the championship on 6 February 2003 in Iowa City, by the fed's own title history; the president boasts of it a week later ("Last week, I gave you a champion!"). Lost it at Revolution to Jason Dread, after pulling the referee into a charging opponent and then bringing the belt itself into the match (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).
note: The fed's own opening montage at Revolution says the belt had been returned to him during a Lockdown a month or so earlier; its title history records the same as an award on 6 February 2003. The one piece of that night held is Scorpion's challenge to him.

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Jason Dread

won.source: The fed's own Revolution script (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

how: Won at Revolution when Enigma laid Blayze out and draped Dread's arm across him; lost it to Legacy at a Lockdown in January 2005 (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/lockdown-results-2005-01.html).
note: The gap between the two dates is the gap in the record, not a claim about a single unbroken reign: nothing is held of the fed at all between June 2003 and December 2004.

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Legacy

won.source: The fed's own Lockdown results (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/lockdown-results-2005-01.html).

how: Beat Jason Dread in the main event and chokeslammed him through a table afterwards; still champion on the card of 3 February 2005, the last thing the fed wrote.

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Tim Inman

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it; he is named the champion in the act of losing it.

how: Lost it to Phil Burner at Showdown I in November 1999, to a man the fed's own history calls his long-time nemesis. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

title: ccw-heavyweight
label: Neurosis

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed the current World Heavyweight Champion in the alliance's own champions block for the fed, on a page whose own Top 10 list for March 2002 says the world title was vacant. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: SOURCES DISAGREE, inside one document: the champions block names him, the same page's own monthly ranking calls the belt vacant and has him tied at number one for it. Both readings are recorded and neither is picked.

title: ccw-hardcore
label: Brad Douglas

won.source: The fed's own hardcore title history (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/hardcore-title-history-2003.html): 02-20-2003, Chicago, Ill.

how: Won it on 20 February 2003 in Chicago, beating Gabe Nyte, Jack Manson and RHSC, by the fed's own title history; billed "CCW's Hardcore Champion" in the fed's own magazine of 1 March 2003 (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/ccw-in-demand-news-2003-03.html) and still carrying the belt to the ring on 6 March.
note: By the pay-per-view three weeks later the belt is on Jack Manson, and nothing held says how it got there.

title: ccw-hardcore
label: Enigma

won.source: The fed's own Revolution script (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

how: Beat Jack Manson in a match fought with barbed wire, a trash can and a board of nails; the rematch at the Lockdown of 10 April 2003 ended without a winner, the broadcast calling it a no contest after Adam Christ and Blayze both interfered (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/lockdown-results-2003-04-10.html).

title: ccw-hardcore
label: Scorpion

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed the fed's own Hardcore Champion in the alliance's champions block and tenth on its own March 2002 ranking. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

title: ccw-hardcore
label: Jack Manson

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it; he is billed the champion in the act of losing it.

how: Lost it to Enigma in Revolution's opening match (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

won.source: Won the title from Jim "Klown" Bowe on the promotion's own 'Friday Fury' broadcast by submission.

title: ccw-independent
label: Scorpion

won.source: The fed's own match board, the final of its Independent title tournament (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/match-scorpion-vs-yama-tatsu-2003-03-06.html).

how: Won the vacant championship in the final of the fed's own tournament on 6 March 2003, pinning Yama Tatsu and Kyle Thorne together after a Tail Whip onto a chair; kept it against Michael Stevens on 13 March (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/match-scorpion-vs-stevens-2003-03-13.html) and against Dan Logan in a leather-strap match at Revolution (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).
note: The tournament opened on the Lockdown of 13 February 2003; the fed's own title history page for the belt, as it survives, lists no champion since the fed's reinstatement that February.

title: ccw-womens
label: Sheena Ramone

won.source: The fed's own Revolution script (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

how: Won by disqualification, which the fed's own ring announcer declared a title change on the spot.

title: ccw-womens
label: Devyl

won.source: Nothing held records when or how she won it.

how: Billed the fed's own Women's Champion in the alliance's champions block. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: Her own roster card claims four reigns with this championship and an award for the longest of them; this is the only one the record dates at all.

title: ccw-womens
label: Lacey Skye Morris

won.source: Nothing held records when or how she won it; she is billed the champion in the act of losing it.

how: Lost it to Sheena Ramone at Revolution, by disqualification (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

title: ccw-trans-atlantic
label: Michael "Spitfire" Stevens

won.source: The fed's own Revolution script (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

how: Won a three-way against Gobstopper and Ace Hawk at Revolution, announced as the new champion.
note: The fed's own newsdesk of 29 March 2003 billed the three-way as reinstating the championship to crown a new champion (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/ccw-news-2003-03-29-to-2003-04-11.html); Ace Hawk came into it as the announced number-one contender (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/match-hawk-vs-gobstopper-2003.html).

title: ccw-trans-atlantic
label: The Valiant One

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed the fed's own Trans-Atlantic Champion in the alliance's champions block. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: SOURCES DISAGREE: the same page's own Top 10 list for March 2002 gives the championship to Brad Lamen instead. Both are recorded.

title: ccw-trans-atlantic
label: Brad Lamen

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed "Brad Lamen(Trans Atlantic Champion)", second on the fed's own Top 10 list for March 2002. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: The same page's champions block gives the belt to The Valiant One. The two claims sit on one page and neither is preferred here.

title: ccw-tag-team
label: Adam Christ & Jack Manson

won.source: The fed's own Revolution script (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/revolution-2003.html).

how: Won the vacant championship in a three-team ladder match at Revolution, Christ pinning Damien Nhyte; the two took the belts and left through the crowd without waiting to be announced.
note: On the Lockdown of 10 April 2003 the two announced a contract renaming the belts the CCW Extreme Titles, to be defended under hardcore rules while they held them, and named their team Misunderstood (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/lockdown-results-2003-04-10.html).

title: ccw-tag-team
label: The Blood Brothers

won.source: Nothing held records when or how they won them.

how: Billed the fed's own Tag Team Champions, "The Blood Brothers(Benny Blades & Neurosis)", in the alliance's champions block. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: By the spring of 2003 the championship was vacant and the fed ran a tournament for it; nothing held covers the years between.

title: ccw-pacific
label: John Jupiter

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed the fed's own Pacific Champion in the alliance's champions block and third on its own March 2002 ranking. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).
note: The championship itself appears nowhere else in the held record.

title: ccw-independent
label: Kensuke Suzahara

won.source: Nothing held records when or how he won it.

how: Billed the fed's own Independent Champion in the alliance's champions block and fourth on its own March 2002 ranking. Primetime Central's own member profile for the fed (/promotions/ptc/archive/ccw-profile-2002.html).

title: ccw-independent
label: Jim "Klown" Bowe

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own card billing as reigning champion entering his 10 December 1999 defense.

note: Lost the title to Ricky Coyote on the promotion's own 'Friday Fury' broadcast.

title: ccw-tag-team
label: The Disciples

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own card billing as reigning champions entering their 10 December 1999 defense.

note: Retained the titles against The Pogui Warriors on the promotion's own 'Friday Fury' broadcast.

title: ccw-lightweight
label: El Mierda

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own preview-card billing as reigning champion heading into a 12 December 1999 defense.

note: Billed to defend the title against Scotty the Hotty; no surviving document confirms the outcome.

title: ccw-womens
label: Kelly Bowe

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own preview-card billing as reigning champion heading into a 12 December 1999 defense.

note: Billed to defend the title against Delilah; no surviving document confirms the outcome.
